summary: Coinbase shares rose more than 60% in November 2023, their second-best month since the 2021 listing, as rivals FTX and Binance faced criminal fallout. Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted and Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty, while Binance saw outflows and falling market share. Analysts see potential share gains for Coinbase but also a threat from spot bitcoin ETFs, even as the SEC fight continues.
one_line: Coinbase stock surged over 60% in November 2023 as FTX's Bankman-Fried and Binance's Zhao faced prison, though spot bitcoin ETFs and SEC cases loom.
key_facts: Coinbase shares rose more than 60% in November 2023, its second-best monthly performance since going public in 2021, and climbed more than 250% in the first 11 months of 2023.
In 2022 Coinbase lost 86% of its value amid soaring inflation and rising interest rates.
Sam Bankman-Fried was found guilty of seven criminal fraud counts on Nov. 2 after a monthlong trial; he is scheduled to be sentenced in March.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty on Nov. 21 to Bank Secrecy Act violations and agreed to step down as CEO; sentencing is set for February, with guidelines suggesting 12 to 18 months.
The Justice Department's settlement with Binance was $4.3 billion; customers pulled more than $1 billion in the first 24 hours and liquidity dropped 25%, per Kaiko.
Binance's market share fell from over 60% in February to under 50% in September, per CoinGecko, and its trading volume fell by two-thirds between the first and third quarters.
Coinbase is the fourth-biggest global exchange by daily volume, the only one publicly traded in the U.S., with a market cap of close to $30 billion.
Mizuho said Coinbase shares were up about 20% since Zhao's settlement; it raised its price target to $35 from $31 while keeping an underperform rating.
Coinbase shares fell 2.4% to $124.72 on Thursday.
Bittrex announced on Nov. 20 that all trading on Bittrex Global would be disabled effective Dec. 4; the SEC had charged Bittrex and its ex-CEO in April with operating an unregistered exchange.
Bitcoin accounted for 38% of Coinbase's third-quarter transaction volume and almost the same percentage of revenue.
BlackRock, WisdomTree and Invesco have filed with the SEC for spot bitcoin ETFs; BlackRock, Franklin Templeton and WisdomTree picked Coinbase for custody services.
JPMorgan analysts (neutral rating, $80 target) said ETFs help Coinbase short term but could cause fee pressure and fewer accounts longer term.
Coinbase and Binance still face SEC legal battles, and Coinbase executives have floated leaving the U.S. if no resolution is reached.
